engine.title: The multibagger screen qualified nobody for four weeks
engine.body: Corrects what this entry said on 2026-08-27. It read ‘the scan is running on schedule’ and blamed the fixed list on cadence. The ledger says otherwise: the last multibagger row is 2026-08-01, while magic, magicmagic and ai_longterm — the same Saturday job, the same slot — all logged 2026-08-22. Twenty-six days, three Saturdays, nothing written.
engine.note: The screen is not broken. Run on 2026-08-27 it took 11 candidates and rejected 10 for R:R below 2.0 — CHENNPETRO 1.29, FLUOROCHEM 1.07, GLAXO 0.59, which needs a 63% win rate merely to break even. The defect was that a week qualifying nobody wrote nothing at all, so the page served the 1 August list as though it were current. The attempt is recorded either way now. The gate is NOT loosened: publishing a 0.59 R:R to keep the section busy is the exact trade this screen exists to refuse, and an empty week is a real result.

engine.title: Stop buying strength that has already run
engine.body: The 4H RSI ceiling for longs was 75. Splitting every closed trade by the RSI recorded at entry showed the engine bleeding above 65 and profitable below it. The ceiling is now 65.
engine.note: Holds in both halves of the sample and at every cut point tested (60, 65, 70), so it is not one lucky threshold. The threshold was still chosen from this sample, so treat the size as an upper bound.

engine.title: A break-even stop would not have helped
engine.body: The median losing trade was +1.44R in profit before it reversed, and 59% touched a full +1R first. That looks like an obvious fix: move the stop to entry once price pays 1R. Re-walking every trade bar by bar, with winners subject to the same rule, says otherwise.
engine.note: The first version of this test only altered losers, which guarantees a positive answer. Correcting it reversed the conclusion. Nothing tested cleared one standard error, so no stop rule was adopted.

engine.title: Trades were being closed at prices that never traded
engine.body: The grader had never resolved a single trade — an exception was being swallowed silently — leaving a fallback path that could book an exit at a bar from before the signal existed. Every closed trade was re-graded against bars that actually printed.
evidence: exits corrected to a real price
engine.note: This moved the headline number against me. It is published anyway, because the earlier number was not real. Pre-correction data is kept in the repo rather than deleted.

engine.title: A first target must pay back the risk
engine.body: T1 was whichever structural level sat nearest the entry, with no distance test. One signal shipped a T1 worth 0.19R against its own stop, printed beside an R:R of 2.41 quoted off T2. T1 must now return at least 1R.

chess.title: Strategy: Open Files for Rooks
chess.body: Rooks need open files to be active. An open file has no pawns. A semi-open file has only enemy pawns. Double rooks on an open file (called 'Rooks on 7th') is a deadly battery. Strategy: open files by pawn trades, then occupy them immediately. Don't leave your rooks passive on the back rank.

wisdom.title: Regulate Yourself First
wisdom.body: You cannot be a calm parent if you're running on stress, sleep debt, and financial anxiety. Your regulation is their regulation — babies co-regulate with caregivers. Deep breath before you pick her up. Shoulders down. Slow exhale. Your nervous system sets the tone for the room.

book.author: Peter Thiel
book.lesson: Thiel's most contrarian idea: competition is not virtuous. Monopoly is. Competitive markets destroy profit margins as businesses race to the bottom on price. A monopoly earns outsized profits because it has no competition. Google has 90%+ search market share and 25%+ net margins. A restaurant in a crowded market has 5% margins. Thiel argues: don't compete. Create something so different that you have no competition. Ask not 'how do I beat my competitors?' but 'how do I build something where there are no competitors?'
book.key_quote: If you are competing, you are not monopolising. If you are not monopolising, you are not building a truly great business.
book.action: Ask about your current work or business: who are my direct competitors? If you have many, that's a warning sign. Find the niche where you can be the only one.
crux: Progress is either 0→1 (new things) or 1→n (copying). Copying does not create new value.
The contrarian question: what important truth do very few people agree with you on?
Competition is for losers. Perfect competition drives profit to zero by definition.
Monopoly is the condition of every genuinely valuable business. All happy companies are different.
Four monopoly traits: proprietary technology, network effects, economies of scale, branding.
Proprietary tech must be 10x better than the alternative, not marginally better.
Start with a small market you can dominate, then expand. Big markets are a red flag.
Last-mover advantage beats first-mover. What matters is the last big cash flow.
Power law: one investment returns more than all others combined. This applies to careers too.
Definite optimism builds the future. Indefinite optimism just expects it to arrive.
Sales matters as much as product, and engineers systematically underrate it.
Seven questions every business must answer: engineering, timing, monopoly, people, distribution, durability, secret.
Secrets still exist. The belief that everything is known is why so little gets found.
Founders should ask: will this still be valuable in 10 years?
learnings: If you're competing on the same axis as everyone else, the margin is already gone.
Small dominated market first. Broad ambition second.
Power laws mean concentration beats diversification for effort allocation.
Distribution is not an afterthought. A product nobody hears about does not exist.
examples: PayPal targeted eBay power sellers — 20,000 people — rather than 'online payments'. Domination first, expansion after.
Google has held roughly two-thirds of search since 2002 and prints margins that a competitive market would have erased.
Facebook started at one university with 100% of that market, then expanded campus by campus.
adapt: Codex's edge is not 'AI automation'. It is a specific workflow for a specific buyer at $47. Dominate that.
The faceless FP&A page competes in a narrower niche than generic finance content. That narrowness is the asset.
10x, not 10%: a signals product must be clearly better than a free Telegram channel, not slightly.
Distribution for the Dubai search is the network, not the CV. Applications without referrals are 1→n.

minimalism.title: Decision Fatigue Is The Real Cost
minimalism.body: A cluttered wardrobe costs you a decision every morning. Obama and Jobs wore the same thing daily for a reason — not style, bandwidth. Every trivial choice you delete is one more available for the choices that matter.
minimalism.action: Choose tomorrow's clothes tonight. Notice the morning it buys back.
minimalism.label: Minimalism

etiquette.title: Ask One More Question
etiquette.body: Most people wait to talk. The one who asks a second follow-up is remembered as the best conversationalist in the room, having said almost nothing.
etiquette.action: Ask a second follow-up before offering your own view.
etiquette.label: Etiquette

stillness.title: Voluntary Discomfort
stillness.body: The Stoics practised poverty deliberately — plain food, cold, hard beds. Not self-punishment. Rehearsal, so that losing comfort stops being frightening.
stillness.action: Cold shower. Or skip one meal. Notice it is survivable.
stillness.label: Stillness

model.title: Bottleneck Theory
model.body: A system moves at the speed of its slowest constraint. Optimising anything else produces zero throughput gain and feels productive, which is why it is so common.
model.action: Identify the real bottleneck in your week. Work only on that.
model.label: Mental Model

drill.title: Recall, Don't Reread
drill.body: Close the material and write what you remember. Retrieval builds memory; rereading builds only the feeling of knowing, which is why students who reread do worse.
drill.action: Close the last thing you studied. Write everything you recall. Then check.
drill.label: Drill

health.title: VO2max Is The Strongest Predictor
health.body: Cardiorespiratory fitness predicts all-cause mortality better than smoking status, blood pressure, or cholesterol. Moving from the bottom quartile to merely above-average is the single largest risk reduction available to you — larger than any drug.
health.action: One 20-minute session where holding a conversation is difficult.
health.label: Health

quote.name: Patrick Collison
quote.quote: Move with urgency and focus. The world rewards those who ship.

lesson.lesson: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.

case.title: Alibaba: Jack Ma's 1001st Try
case.story: Jack Ma was rejected from Harvard 10 times. KFC rejected him. Failed at multiple businesses. Alibaba launched in 1999 and became a $600B company.
case.lesson: Resilience is the most under-rated competitive advantage. Most people quit. The gap between failure and success is usually just one more attempt.

fpna.title: Power BI for FP&A
fpna.body: Replace Excel pivots. Connect to ERP source. Saves 5+ hours/month on month-end decks.

cfo.title: CFO Step 4: Board Communication
cfo.body: CFOs present to the Board. Boards want: Are we on budget? What's the cash position? What risks keep you up at night? Practice speaking to non-finance people. Remove jargon. Lead with the conclusion, not the workings.

money_hack.body: Sovereign Gold Bonds: 2.5% interest + gold price appreciation. No storage cost.

dubai.title: The stack that clears AED 30K
dubai.body: CA or ACCA, plus SAP or Oracle, plus Power BI, plus IFRS 9 and 16. That is the whole gate. Miss one and you are competing on price.
dubai.targets: Targets: ADNOC · Emirates · Majid Al Futtaim · DP World · FAB · Emaar.
dubai.action: Put "IFRS 16 implementation" and "rolling forecast" in the cover letter. Recruiters grep for exactly those two strings.

desk.productivity: Write tomorrow's top 3 tasks tonight. Wake up with a plan.

father.title: Put her in front of a mirror
father.do: Hold her at a mirror and name both of you.
father.why: Self-recognition does not arrive until around 18 months, so she is currently treating the reflection as another baby — which is exactly why it holds her attention and drives social behaviours.

father.title: Ask her mother what she needs
father.do: Ask directly, once, and act on the answer without negotiating it.
father.why: The most reliable predictor of a child's early environment is the functioning of the partnership around them. This is a fatherhood task, not a marital one.

life_wisdom.teaching: Reality has more facets than any single viewpoint can hold. The classic image is blind men describing an elephant — each is accurate and each is incomplete.
life_wisdom.apply: In a disagreement, state the other person's position better than they did before you argue against it. If you cannot, you have not understood it yet.

life_wisdom.teaching: Impermanence is usually offered as consolation in difficulty. It applies symmetrically: the good quarter, the promotion, the peak are equally conditioned.
life_wisdom.apply: On a good week, note it explicitly and hold it lightly. The habit of not over-identifying with wins is what makes losses survivable.

speaking.title: Kill the upspeak on numbers
speaking.drill: Say ten figures aloud, dropping pitch on the last syllable of each.
speaking.why: Rising pitch on a number makes it sound like an estimate. You rarely want that.

interview_tech.q: What is ROIC and why would a CFO care more than about net margin?
interview_tech.a: ROIC = NOPAT ÷ invested capital. Net margin tells you profitability per rupee of sales; ROIC tells you profitability per rupee of capital committed — which is the only question when you are deciding where to put the next AED 50M. A 3% margin business turning capital four times beats an 8% margin business turning it once. In retail this is exactly the discount-versus-premium format argument, and it is why space productivity matters more than headline margin.

interview_tech.q: How do you test goodwill for impairment, and why does retail make it harder?
interview_tech.a: Goodwill is not amortised — it is tested annually at the cash-generating unit level. Compare the CGU's carrying amount to its recoverable amount, the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use. Retail is harder for two reasons: defining the CGU, because a single store may not generate independent cash inflows once you have click-and-collect and online returns routed through it; and the discount rate, because store-level risk differs from group WACC. Auditors challenge the growth rate beyond year five hardest — keep it at or below long-run GDP for the market.
interview_tech.who: Big Four · Majid Al Futtaim · Tesco

interview_soft.q: Why do you want to be a CFO, and why in retail?
interview_soft.a: Structure: motive, evidence, specificity. Weak answers say 'growth' and 'leadership'. Strong answer names the work: 'I want the seat where capital allocation is decided, not just reported. In FP&A I model the store investment case; the CFO decides which twelve of thirty get built. Retail because the feedback loop is daily — you see whether the decision worked in the sales line the next week, which is not true in most industries.' Then one proof point with a number attached.

interview_soft.q: How do you build a finance team, and how do you handle an underperformer?
interview_soft.a: Building: hire for one clear gap, not a generalist; define what good looks like in writing before the first review, not after. Underperformance: the honest answer is that you probably waited too long once, and learned from it. Structure — early specific feedback with examples, an agreed plan with dates, documented check-ins, and a decision at the end of it either way. The failure mode they are probing for is a manager who avoids the conversation and lets the team carry someone for a year.
